materials.title: The painting I nearly hid
materials.text:
At our school art sale, I displayed three finished paintings and left a fourth under the table. It showed a harbour at dawn, but the boats were only pencil ____1____. I had never added their colours.

A visitor noticed its corner. Before she could pull it out, I said, "That one isn't ____2____."

"May I look anyway?"

I showed it to her, explaining where I had stopped. She studied it more ____3____ than she had studied the finished pictures. I expected a list of faults.

Instead, she asked why I had chosen that view. I described sitting beside my grandfather, peacefully watching the sky brighten while the boats remained dark. As I spoke, I remembered the ____4____ that had made me start painting.

The visitor said the pencil lines helped her imagine how the picture had ____5____. Her son was learning to draw and often believed that a good painting appeared perfectly at the first attempt. She wanted him to see a stage ____6____ the beginning and the finished work.

I offered to add the colours before she collected it. She ____7____, taking a moment before answering. "Only if you want to. Please don't finish it just to make it look more expensive."

We agreed on a small price and wrote a note clearly identifying it as a work in ____8____. I did not want anybody to mistake it for something I had completed.

After she left, I took a photograph for my records. The empty space no longer looked simply like ____9____. It showed a choice I had not yet made.

I still finish most of my paintings. But I have stopped ____10____ every incomplete page as though it proves I cannot draw. Some are useful studies; others need another attempt. What matters is being ____11____ about their stage and purpose.

The sale did not turn unfinished work into an excuse to avoid ____12____. It helped me see that learning has visible ____13____. A visitor had asked a better question than "Is it finished?" She had asked how it ____14____. That conversation gave me the courage to put a sketchbook on the table at the next sale, with its working pages ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Uncoloured boats are pencil outlines. Receipts, prices and names are not the drawn boat shapes.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The narrator stopped before adding colour, so the painting is not finished. Weight, fame and a frame do not describe that incomplete stage.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Studying and asking about the picture show careful attention. Anger, brevity and secrecy are not supported.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Remembering the peaceful dawn with Grandfather restores the feeling that motivated the painting. A deadline, address and price are not the personal experience described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Pencil lines reveal how the painting developed. Disappeared and sold concern loss or transaction, and travelled movement rather than creation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: An unfinished study is a stage between starting and completion. Above, against and outside do not express that sequence.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Taking a moment before answering explicitly shows hesitation. Hurried and cheered do not fit that pause; she qualifies the offer rather than simply refusing it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Work in progress is the standard phrase for an unfinished piece. Silence, danger and secret do not name its stage.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The narrator stops seeing incompletion as failure. Decoration, movement and colour do not capture the earlier negative self-judgment.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The opening hidden painting motivates no longer hiding incomplete pages. Measuring, selling and signing are not the avoided display behaviour.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Clearly labelling its stage is honesty. Speed and silence are irrelevant, and certainty does not specify truthful representation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Valuing studies is not an excuse to avoid effort on work. Attention is something the narrator wanted, travel unrelated and payment a buyer action.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The comparison shows visible stages of learning. Owners, prices and rules do not describe creative development.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Her question about the chosen view reveals how the work began. Cost and weight are not the discussion, and the work has not ended.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: A sketchbook displayed with working pages open makes the process visible. Locked or lost prevents viewing, while empty contradicts the working pages.

materials.title: Two kinds of directions
materials.text:
Grandpa asked me to help him use the new ticket machine at the station. He usually bought tickets from a person, but wanted to ____1____ the machine himself.

I explained the screens ____2____, pointing at one button after another. He asked me to ____3____ the first step. I sighed and reached forward to do it for him.

"I'm trying to learn," he said.

His quiet words stopped me. I had mistaken being fast for being helpful. Grandpa looked ____4____ because I had given several instructions before he could try the first one.

I stepped back and ____5____ him one action. Then I waited while he tried it ____6____. When he selected the wrong screen, we returned to the start. I explained more ____7____ instead of taking over.

After one more ____8____, he bought the correct ticket. The machine was not suddenly ____9____, but he now knew where to begin. He kept the ticket and suggested a short walk before the train arrived.

Outside, I could not find the path to the old bridge. Grandpa ____10____ it clearly, pointing to a narrow lane beside a café. He had walked there long before the station entrance moved.

I was ____11____ by how easily our roles had changed. At the machine, I had knowledge he needed. Outside, his experience guided me. Neither kind made the other person's ____12____ unimportant.

On the bridge, I thanked him for reminding me to show ____13____ when helping. He smiled. "Then explain the machine again on the way back," he said. "Just a little more ____14____."

We laughed. Next time he would try without me beside him. That afternoon, however, we had found our way ____15____, each giving the other enough time to understand.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Grandpa wants to use or manage the machine independently. Repair, sale and concealment are not his purpose.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Many buttons explained before the first attempt and the request to repeat show excessive speed. Secrecy, anger and silence do not describe the explanation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: He needs the first step said again. Forgetting, skipping and cancelling it do not support learning.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Too many instructions leave him confused. Pride and certainty conflict with his need for repetition, and boredom is not the described obstacle.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The narrator demonstrates one action, so showed. Promising alone does not demonstrate it, while selling and borrowing do not fit the instruction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: He tries it himself. Myself would refer to the narrator; ourselves/themselves are plural.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Waiting through errors rather than taking over demonstrates patience. Volume, brevity and secrecy do not express the changed attitude.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Another wrong selection is a mistake before success. Ticket is the eventual result, journey the travel and promise unrelated.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: One successful attempt does not make the new machine fully familiar. It is not broken, price-changing or empty as a result of learning.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: He gives clear directions to the lane and bridge, so explained. Ignoring, blocking and forgetting would not guide the narrator.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The easy exchange of expert roles surprises the narrator. The text describes appreciation rather than offence, disappointment or shame.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Both people need to learn in different situations. Clothing, ticket and age are not the reciprocal process valued here.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Giving a learner time respects their effort. Speed caused the problem, fear is not a helping principle and silence alone would not teach the steps.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Grandpa jokes that the explanation should be slower. Price, formality and privacy do not address the initial rushed instructions.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: They help one another find their way together. They are neither upstairs nor abroad, and the final scene is explicitly not alone.
